title: Adaptive Tenant Fairness Controller with Soft Preemption and Priority Metering
creator: Priya Shah
description: Design and implement an admission controller for dedicated fleets that enforces per-tenant throughput guarantees while enabling burst envelopes and a soft preemption path for graceful degradation. The controller coordinates with autoscaling signals and the existing token-reservation layer to provide predictable minimum throughput, tenant fairness during contention, and observable degradation behavior when capacity is constrained.
background_and_rationale: Customers running Dedicated pools need predictable throughput guarantees for committed tenants, but real workloads are bursty and multi-tenant fleets face transient overloads. Current admission behavior either accepts all requests until the runtime becomes overloaded or rejects aggressively, causing poor tail latency for high-priority traffic. This initiative introduces a hybrid policy: token-share-backed minimum guarantees + per-tenant burst envelopes + a soft preemption path that first deprioritizes and queues, then sheds low-priority requests if needed. Integrates autoscaler headroom signals to avoid oscillatory shedding.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant minimum throughput (tokens/sec) can be configured and enforced in the admission controller
Burst envelopes allow tenants to exceed their baseline for short periods and decay according to configurable windowing
Soft preemption flow: (1) move to low-priority lane + longer queue timeout, (2) apply incremental shedding for best-effort requests, (3) preserve critical SLOs for guaranteed tenants
Controller consumes autoscaler headroom and pending-inflight metrics to avoid triggering preemption during safe scale-up windows
Unit and integration tests cover steady-state, burst, and recovery scenarios under synthetic load
Dashboard panels show per-tenant admitted rate, queue depth, shed rate, and time-to-recover after an overload
Canary rollout with gradual traffic weighting and automated rollback on SLO regressions
engineering_notes: Coordination points: admission controller library sits in routing service; token reservation changes are required to expose per-tenant shares and burst budget introspection

Policy math: use leaky-bucket for baseline token issuance and a second exponential-decay burst budget. When total outstanding demand > capacity, compute per-tenant shortfall and apply proportional shedding on best-effort requests.
Soft preemption strategy: first lower scheduling priority and extend queue TTL by 50-200ms, then move to probabilistic dropper on low-priority classes at p=0.1..0.7 depending on deficit magnitude
Autoscaler integration: subscribe to scale-pending and available-headroom signals (metrics exported by fleet-autoscaler) to suppress preemption for a 30s hold window while scaling completes
Performance budget: decision path must add <150us p95 overhead to admission for 99% of requests. Implement hot-path in C++ code path; provide Go shim for control plane only.
Observability: expose metrics tenant.admit_count, tenant.shed_count, tenant.queue_latency, controller.decision_latency; correlate with SLO traces in tracing service
Backward compatibility: default to current admission behavior unless tenant has a policy attached; rollout flag controlled in console and via feature-gate env var
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed — simulated multi-tenant bursts in local harness; validated token-share math for simple proportional shedding (notes in design doc)
2026-03-04: Prototype admission hook implemented in routing service; added unit tests for baseline token issuance and burst decay
2026-03-06: Performance profiling shows 120us median extra latency; optimizing lock contention in the shared budget map
2026-03-08: Design review with PM and Design — requested clearer UX for configuring burst windows and a 'protect critical endpoints' checkbox; added to acceptance criteria
2026-03-10: Opened draft PR for the admission controller core: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/411 (WIP). Added integration test harness that drives autoscaler headroom signals
test_plan: Unit tests for token issuer, burst-decay, and proportional shedding math
Integration tests in CI that replay production-like traffic traces (trace subset: tenant mix, seq lengths) and assert SLO preservation for guaranteed tenants
Chaos test: inject delayed autoscaler signals and verify hold-window prevents premature shedding
Canary: stage on a small dedicated fleet with two tenants (1 guaranteed, 1 best-effort) and run a 48h workload while monitoring shed_rate and tail latency
Post-deploy audit: compare billing/usage to ensure no regressions in cost accounting for tenants
rollout_and_mitigation: Rollout uses feature-flag per-tenant. Start with non-critical tenants in canary cluster, 10% traffic, 12h evaluation windows
Automated SLO monitor will trigger rollback if guaranteed-tenant p99 latency increases >20% or shed_rate for guaranteed class >0
Mitigation path: disable soft preemption and fall back to current token-reservation + strict-drop policy; escalate to on-call runtime engineer
Post-rollout follow-ups: tune burst decay constants and default envelope sizes based on observed tenant behavior
